_comment: GENERATED by `python3 -m edge_workbench.prepare`. Do not edit:
re-run it. This is what the build reads instead of the
tutorial, so that a build depends on files in this repository
and not on which branch a sibling checkout happens to be on.
`source.sha` is the commit the tutorial was read at. A gate
compares it against the tutorial's head to tell you when the
tutorial has moved and this needs re-running.
`gaps` lists what the tutorial does not state in a form this
step can read. Those are the model-assisted half's input; an
empty list means the tutorial said everything itself.

example.quote: Take the four-vertex directed graph with edges

meanings.E01: Each vertex's best offer this round: the shortest route to it using one more edge.
meanings.E02: Which vertices improve: the offer beats their known distance, and any first arrival counts.
meanings.E03: The new, shorter distances, only at the vertices that improved.
meanings.E04: Improved vertices take their new distance; every other vertex keeps its old one.
meanings.init: Only the source starts with a distance, 0; every other vertex starts unreached.
meanings.stop: A full round changed no distance, so these are the shortest distances.

tensorNotes.G: the graph: G[s, d] is the weight of the edge s -> d
tensorNotes.D: the distances; infinity marks a vertex not yet reached
tensorNotes.N: the relaxed candidate distances for this round
tensorNotes.C: the improvement mask: where a candidate beats the current distance
tensorNotes.NewlyRelaxed: the candidates that actually improved a distance

quotes.E01: vertex with a finite distance is relaxed again every round
quotes.E02: comparison yields True exactly where the new candidate is strictly smaller than
quotes.E03: candidates that actually improved a distance
quotes.E04: improved vertices take their new distance
quotes.init: Initialization sets the source distance to $0$; every other vertex
quotes.stop: The cascade halts when a full round of

E01.graph: Try relaxing every edge into $d$, and keep the minimum candidate distance.
E01.einsum: For each destination vertex $d$, the output tensor element $N_{i,d}$ is computed by considering every possible predecessor $s$. For each such $s$, we form the candidate value $D_{i,s} + G_{s,d}$. We then take the minimum over all $s$.

E02.graph: If the new relaxed value improves the distance to $d$, update it; otherwise keep the old distance.
E02.einsum: Take an elementwise less-than between two tensors over $d$.

E03.graph: Keep the new candidate distance only at the vertices that improved.

E04.graph: Improved vertices take their new distance, and every other vertex keeps its current one.
E04.einsum: Take $NewlyRelaxed_{i,d}$ where it is present, and otherwise carry $D_{i,d}$ forward.
